No invariance or measurement-error study is reported.

models.section: 6. Model Two: Leaf Distribution and Leaf Shape
models.purpose: Relate leaf major-axis length and internode distance to shaded-area fraction under solar altitude.

objectives: Minimize shaded-area fraction and infer a relationship among spacing, shape, and solar altitude.

Leaves are horizontal and ipsilateral.
Leaf area is fixed while shape changes.
Solar altitude is fixed within each derivation.

details: E=0 at h=h_0; the h<h_0 case produces positive overlap in the intended domain.

parameter_estimation.method: Leaf length and internode distance are measured for three species; solar altitude is inferred and converted to latitude.

steps: Choose a region and solar altitude.
Represent the leaf by a fixed-area rhombus.
Evaluate overlap ratio.

Convert inferred solar altitude to latitude for three species.
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Closed-form calculation; no numerical convergence criterion is applicable.

assumptions: Leaf distribution minimizes overlap.
Two-leaf single-branch geometry represents crown distribution.
Sun exposure dominates other leaf-shape drivers.
Annual representative solar altitude occurs at noon on the vernal equinox.

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: The three measured pairs cannot identify a causal leaf-distribution law, and the model uses broad latitude ranges as validation.

strengths: Names output, control variable, regimes, and boundary case.
Produces a directly testable external prediction.
limitations: The first and second overlap equations are algebraically consistent only if the undeclared L equals L_major.
The latitude table has three cases and at least one malformed true range.
The biological optimality premise is untested.
Branch and crown interactions are omitted.
